company is going to charge you in addition to a percent management fee. So, before I let you go,
couple keys to success when it comes to building your team and dealing with people in your
development business. Communicate your expectations as clearly as you possibly can. The more
clearly you can communicate your expectations about uh timing, about quality of work, about
quality of communication and responsiveness, the less problems you're going to have. Even though
your job is to hire great people for your team, it's your job as a developer to drive the vision
forward. So, you have to be the one that proactively communicates with your team, coordinates
different parts of your team together, gets them on the same page. You have to be the project
manager here. Do not wait for other people to push the ball downfield and assume that they're
making you their first priority because likely they won't. You've got to be the one driving the
ball downfield, communicating your vision, and make sure that your team executes your vision.
Don't nickel and dime people. Don't feel like every time somebody quotes you a fee, you have to
negotiate with them. Sometimes people will quote you fair numbers, fair fees. If you develop a
reputation as somebody that nickel and dimes everyone every single time and beats them up,
people will stop picking up your phone call. People will stop working for you. People will stop
making you their priority, and they will put you at the bottom of the list. These are
professionals. They've spent years studying, learning, paying their dues to develop their
expertise. Pay them accordingly because they are worth it. Respect their time. Respect the time
that they've invested into becoming professionals, and make sure other people eat. It's not your
job as a business person. It's not your job as a developer to squeeze every penny from everybody
else. You're going to do well. Make sure the people that you work with do well as well. And then
pay people on time. Always. Nobody likes chasing down invoices. If you develop a reputation for
somebody that doesn't pay your time on time or tries to renegotiate last minute before it's time
to pay somebody, people will stop picking up the phone for you, and you will lose great team
members. Okay? So, lastly, where do you start? Who do you add to your team first from the list
